gaps.sentence: Club ___ (MEMBER) costs fifty euros a year.
gaps.explanation: "Membership costs" — the fee noun, not the person.

gaps.sentence: The government wants to ___ the tax system (SIMPLE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: simplify means to make simple. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: The trip gave us a lot of ___ (PLEASE).
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of' needs a noun: pleasure (note the irregular spelling).

gaps.sentence: It was the most ___ (FORGET) trip of my life.
gaps.hint: negative adjective: too good to forget
gaps.explanation: 'Unforgettable' = impossible to forget; 'forgetful' describes a person who forgets.

gaps.sentence: Her suitcase was ___ , so the airline charged extra (WEIGHT).
gaps.hint: weighing too much — that is why she paid extra (over-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means too much: overweight explains the extra charge.

gaps.sentence: Mozart was the greatest ___ (MUSIC) of his age.
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ian forms the person: music becomes musician.

gaps.sentence: The delay was caused by a simple ___ (UNDERSTAND).
gaps.hint: negative noun needed: they understood wrongly (mis-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrongly: a misunderstanding is a failure to understand correctly.
After 'complete' a noun is needed: darkness (-ness noun of 'dark').
